On Phu Quoc, a sure bet.
Aug 2026 • Couples
The restaurant is undoubtedly the strong point. The cuisine is more than excellent (they produce many things, sauces and pepper to die for). The dishes are very hearty. 
The pool with a view of the sea is spacious (there are even two of them). The beach (in August = high tide) is tiny, but acceptable compared to the others on the island this season, which are almost non-existent. 
The rooms are spacious (112 facing the restaurant) and well-equipped. The A/C is efficient and makes no noise. 
The staff is very helpful and attentive. The breakfast offers a wide, unlimited selection with a new local dish option every day. 
The hotel rents scooters for a little more, but with a full tank included. 
200 m away, Sunset Beach allows you to listen to music and watch a pyrotechnic show on the beach every evening. 
Hotel is 10 minutes away by scooter or GRAB from a night market.

A Classy, Charming, Vegan-Friendly Spot You’ll Return To
Feb 2026 • Couples
The Spice House is a charming gem tucked within the tranquil grounds of the refined Cassia Cottage retreat, hidden away from the bustling main road of Duong Dong town on Phu Quoc’s west coast. It’s one of the few truly five-star standard accommodations along that strip, and also easily accessible from the beach if you stroll by from any of the nearby properties.

Having stayed a few nights at a neighbouring villa compound with limited dining options, we came to try their vegetarian dinner menu and enjoyed it so much we returned the next day for a late family brunch.

WHAT WE LOVED:

The flavours are clean, the vegetables are full of taste, and the dishes are vibrant with the colours and freshness you expect from Vietnamese fare. While we didn’t sample the Mediterranean options — nourishing soups, salads and pasta — we truly enjoyed every dish from the local selection.

Although the kitchen isn’t purely vegan (meat and seafood appear on the core menu), we were reassured that the restaurant uses no MSG and prepares all sauces in-house, which means less salt and sugar than in many places that offer veggie versions of Vietnamese staples. It’s also an excellent choice for visitors who don’t handle spice well: the fermented chili paste, sesame salt, and a tray of other condiments let you adjust heat and seasoning to your taste.

MUST TRIES:

Being vegan in Asia for nearly two decades, we felt pampered by the sheer choice of plant-based options that were both satisfying and intriguing.

Standouts we reordered on our second visit included the Fried Spring Rolls — a deep-fried indulgence we allow ourselves rarely — golden and crispy with umami-packed, finely shredded vegetables that needed no dipping in the house “fish” sauce and left no greasy aftertaste.

Their House Pho is a must for anyone who appreciates purity of flavour, served with a generous heap of sprouts and fresh herbs. The Heart of Mekong main course is a perfect finish — bold and satisfying without being overwhelming.

The real star was the Crispy Southern Pancake, a spectacle in itself. It arrived on a giant plate and was cut with scissors at the table; you dip rice paper in water, wrap a medley of fresh herbs, pineapple crudités, and pieces of the street-food special, elegantly demonstrated by attentive staff. This dish alone is worth returning for — a fun, engaging way to share food among 4–6 guests.

We also loved the Mushrooms with Phu Quoc green peppercorns, which offered a pleasant tingling warmth from the signature spice. The Owner was present on the floor on both occasions and might engage you in highly amusing conversation.

VALUE FOR MONEY:

For a hungry couple, order three starters and two mains to share and you’ll leave perfectly satisfied with little room for dessert — all for less than $50 (VND 1.2m) without drinks. There’s a cheeky cocktail and mocktail/smoothie selection you can customise.

We had a delicious, much cheaper dinner the night before at a vegan spot in Duong Dong, but The Spice House’s value comes with higher food quality, a lovely ambiance, and friendly, well-trained service.

THE MOOD:

Charming by night yet relaxed by day, the setting is ideal for romantic evenings and laid-back family gatherings. The open-air, poolside all-day diner offers lush garden views and overlooks a coconut palm–fringed beach, making for picturesque sunsets.

Expect to see international guests from the hotel and nearby residences who don’t mind spending a little more than the many affordable options along the road. On a Saturday evening we were among mature, smartly dressed couples respecting the white-tablecloth setting; you may want to reserve in advance.

By contrast, on a Sunday afternoon we almost had the restaurant to ourselves while others chilled under the palms or at the beachfront bar — a perfect spot for a late, peaceful family brunch.

SERVICE:

Service is endearing. Occasional lapses are met with honest smiles, genuine apologies and instant remedies. Not all staff speak English equally well, but orders are repeated to avoid hiccups. Dishes arrived hot and timely; starters were served together and mains followed only after plates were cleared — simple but not always guaranteed elsewhere. Even during busy dinner service, we never had to flag anyone down; the attentive staff checked in more than once to ensure we enjoyed our meal.

ROOM FOR IMPROVEMENT:

If anything could improve, it would be greater ingredient diversity. While each dish had distinct flavours, rewarding textures and picture-friendly presentation, the variety of vegetables and mushrooms felt a bit constrained and repeatable. We didn’t find eggplant, morning glory, or lion’s mane — favourites of ours — and many dishes relied heavily on tofu, which may be an issue for those avoiding soy.

THE BOTTOM LINE:

To this day, Hum in Saigon remains our plant-based restaurant of choice in Vietnam, but The Spice House left a memorable mark: delicious, honest, freshly made plant-based food; a charming setting with a well-matched soundtrack; extremely comfortable seating; and a service team that clearly enjoys interacting with guests. I wish a metropolitan foodie mecca like Hong Kong — where we’ve lived for years — had at least one restaurant like this.

Thank you for looking after our table, Huynh, Quoc, Phuong — we hope to return one day!
